items.readable_text:
Content:
When we need to find the volume of large shapes, it might take a long time to pack the shape with unit cubes and then count them all.

Content:
Instead, many standard shapes have formulas that we can use to quickly calculate their volume. One such shape that has a volume formula is a rectangular prism, such as the one below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/81358b0945c3fb7b1fde8fda5cf7cad7]

Content:
The formula for the volume [MATH: V] of a rectangular prism is
[MATH: V = \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height} .]

Content:
Let's use this formula to find the volume of the rectangular prism below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/43cdd1d768da3a1b0cb30760ad2cbe69]

Content:
This rectangular prism has a length of [MATH: 7], a width of [MATH: 4], and a height of [MATH: 3.]

Content:
So, the volume of the rectangular prism can be found as
[MATH: V|= length × width × height = 7 × 4 × 3 = 84.]

Content:
Therefore, the volume is [MATH: 84] cubic units.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
When we need to find the volume of large shapes, it might take a long time to pack the shape with unit cubes and then count them all.

Content:
Instead, many standard shapes have formulas that we can use to quickly calculate their volume. One such shape that has a volume formula is a rectangular prism, such as the one below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/81358b0945c3fb7b1fde8fda5cf7cad7]

Content:
The formula for the volume [MATH: V] of a rectangular prism is
[MATH: V = \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height} .]

Content:
Let's use this formula to find the volume of the rectangular prism below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/43cdd1d768da3a1b0cb30760ad2cbe69]

Content:
This rectangular prism has a length of [MATH: 7], a width of [MATH: 4], and a height of [MATH: 3.]

Content:
So, the volume of the rectangular prism can be found as
[MATH: V|= length × width × height = 7 × 4 × 3 = 84.]

Content:
Therefore, the volume is [MATH: 84] cubic units.

---

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The volume of the rectangular prism can be found as
[MATH: V|= length × width × height; = 7 × 12 × 2; = 168.]

Finally, note the following:

- The lengths of the prism are measured in feet [MATH: (\text{ft}).]
- Therefore, the volume is measured in cubic feet [MATH: (\text{ft}^3).]

So, we conclude that the prism's volume is [MATH: 168\, \text{ft}^3.]
